newsitem.title: CHILE: CHILE SEC STUDIES ENERSIS DEAL.
newsitem.headline: CHILE SEC STUDIES ENERSIS DEAL.

text.p: Chile's Stocks and Values Superintendency (SVS) said it is studying in detail the $1.5 billion bid by Spanish utility Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA, or Endesa Espana, to take control of power investment company Enersis SA.
"(The SVS) is studying the characteristics of the operation to check that it is in accordance with current legal regulations," SVS superintendent Daniel Yarur told a news conference.

Yarur said, however, that Chilean laws did not specifically cover a deal of the size and complexity of the agreement between Endesa and shareholders in the Chispa group of investment companies, which controls Enersis.
"What must concern us is to make sure that these operations are within the rules of play," said Yarur.
The Chispa investment firms own 29 percent of Enersis, which controls generator Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA (Chile) and distributor Chilectra SA.
